headline: Osia Hyper Retail Limited enters Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process
sum: Osia Hyper Retail Limited, a retail enterprise, has entered the Corporate Insolvency Resolution Process (CIRP) under the Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016. The 5th Committee of Creditors meeting was held on 18 August 2026 to progress the resolution.
implication: Retail sector insolvencies underscore the procedural criticality of CoC consensus in CIRP timelines; counsel should audit secured creditor voting blocs and monitor resolution plan viability against operational cash burn in the first 180-day window.
detail: Osia Hyper Retail Limited, a retail retail entity, initiated formal CIRP proceedings under the IBC 2016. The 5th CoC meeting convened on 18 August 2026 represents progression through the statutory resolution process, which typically operates on a 180-day (extendable to 270-day) timeline from admission. The NSE disclosure confirms Exchange notification of the process commencement, a mandatory requirement under Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements (LODR), 2015.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Section 4 (definition of CIRP), Section 21 (duties of CoC), Section 30 (approval of resolution plan)
framework.note: central - Core statutory architecture; defines CoC composition, voting thresholds (>66% creditors by value for plan approval), and 180/270-day resolution windows.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Section 25 (meetings of the CoC)
framework.note: central - Governs CoC meeting conduct, quorum, voting, and record-keeping; the 5th CoC meeting must comply with these procedures.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Section 23 (resolution professional's duties)
framework.note: central - RP must convene CoC meetings, seek plan proposals, and ensure creditor consensus toward a resolution plan.

framework.ref: Securities and Exchange Board of India (Listing Obligations and Disclosure Requirements) Regulations, 2015 - Regulation 30 (material events and corporate actions)
framework.note: central - Listed companies must disclose CIRP initiation and CoC outcomes to the stock exchange immediately.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Section 31 (approval by the NCLT)
framework.note: central - NCLT review and sanction of the approved resolution plan is the final gating step.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Board of India (Insolvency Resolution Process for Corporate Persons) Regulations, 2016 - Regulation 39 (resolution plan requirements)
framework.note: central - Sets out mandatory contents of a resolution plan, including payment to creditors, management, and ongoing operations.

framework.ref: Insolvency and Bankruptcy Code, 2016 - Section 33 (implementation and closure)
framework.note: Procedural - Governs post-approval execution and discharge of the RP once the plan is implemented.

framework.ref: Companies Act, 2013 - Sections 2(45), 179 (definition of related parties and board disclosure duties)
framework.note: Contextual - Relevant if the resolution plan involves related-party transactions or director-backed bids.

conditions: CoC approval of resolution plan by >66% creditor value (Section 30, IBC 2016)
NCLT sanction of approved plan (Section 31, IBC 2016)
Completion of 180-day resolution window or approved extension to 270 days
approvals: Committee of Creditors (5th meeting convened 18 Aug 2026)
National Company Law Tribunal (NCLT) - post-CoC approval sanction
NSE/stock exchange - mandatory disclosure and monitoring

triggers.note: CIRP admission triggers mandatory 180/270-day resolution window and CoC statutory role in plan selection.
Listed entity CIRP status must be disclosed to NSE/BSE; failure triggers disclosure violation.
Governs RP appointment, CoC formation, plan submission standards, and resolution process transparency.
